title: Grafana + Azure Monitor -- building the pipeline dashboard
exp: With the workspace and identity in place, wire up Azure Monitor as a Grafana data source and build the same panel set from the AWS track, now against Metrics and Log Analytics.
pts: Azure Monitor Metrics query editor requires: resource (or resource group + type), metric namespace, metric name, aggregation -- structurally the same four pieces CloudWatch requires, different field names.
Azure Monitor Logs (KQL) as a Grafana query type: paste KQL directly into a panel. A summarize with a numeric aggregate renders as a time series; a raw project renders as a table/logs view.

Grafana's built-in math expression feature combines multiple queries -- same error-rate-as-percentage pattern as CloudWatch Metric Math, since Azure Monitor has no server-side Metric Math equivalent of its own.
Template variables sourced from a KQL query returning distinct Source_s values populate a $source dropdown -- same purpose as the CloudWatch dimension_values() pattern, different syntax underneath.

Same practical panel set as the AWS dashboard: records per source (Stat), duration trend (Time series), error rate % (Stat, expression), cluster low-CPU signal (Stat), last successful run per source (Table).
pr: Build a Grafana panel using a math expression that computes error rate as a percentage from two Log Analytics KQL queries

qa.q: How does a KQL panel render as a time series instead of a raw table in Grafana?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Include a summarize aggregation with a bin(TimeGenerated, ...) time grouping -- the same requirement as the Logs Insights stats-with-bin() pattern. Without aggregation, Grafana renders raw rows as a table; with a time-bucketed numeric aggregate, it plots as a standard time-series chart.

qa.q: How does Grafana's math expression replicate CloudWatch Metric Math for Azure Monitor, given Azure has no native equivalent?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Define two separate queries (error count, total count), then add a third query as a math expression referencing them by letter: $A / $B * 100. Grafana evaluates this after retrieving both results and renders it as its own panel series -- functionally identical output to CloudWatch Metric Math, just computed client-side in Grafana rather than server-side in the cloud platform, since Azure Monitor itself has no built-in cross-query math feature.
